description: Three keyboard sequencers, each with its own clock, sixteen steps, eight patterns and a three-octave keyboard for setting the note of each step

params.text: Sets how long the pitch takes to slide from the previous note to the new one on a step marked for glide, up to 500ms

inputs.text: A rising edge here advances that row one step; with nothing patched, the row follows the clock of the first row
Adds its voltage to that row's pitch output, transposing the pattern
A rising edge here queues the next pattern for that row, which takes effect when the row reaches its first step
A rising edge here returns every row to the first step of its pattern
A rising edge here queues the next pattern on all three rows
Held above 0V this silences the trigger output of every row and freezes every pitch output at its last note
Held above 0V this silences that row's trigger output and freezes its pitch output at its last note

outputs.text: A 50ms 10V pulse on each step the pattern marks with a note
The pitch of that row's current step, a volt per octave, with the row's octave setting and its V/Oct offset input added

notes: a row plays nothing until a clock is patched to its TRIG input, or to the TRIG input of the first row, which the other two follow when their own is empty
a new module has all sixteen steps of every pattern set to the lowest note with a trigger on each, so clocking it gives a run of one repeated note
clicking a key on a row's keyboard sets the note of the step that row is showing
while a row is paused, right-clicking a key sets the note of the step being shown and moves on to the next step, rolling into the next pattern at the end
while a row is paused, holding Control and right-clicking a key sets that step to change pitch without firing the trigger output
the upper row of marks above a step or pattern strip sets the last one in the run, and the lower row picks which one is shown
menu: Ch 1: Reset Pattern to 1 — makes a trigger at Reset Clk return the first row to its first pattern as well as its first step
Ch 2: Reset Pattern to 1 — makes a trigger at Reset Clk return the second row to its first pattern as well as its first step
Ch 3: Reset Pattern to 1 — makes a trigger at Reset Clk return the third row to its first pattern as well as its first step
